observation.summary: SHIP: the change only renames the private helper _normalise to _normalised_title in src/theseus_reviewer/dedup.py and updates its single call site. fingerprint output is unchanged, and no references to the old name remain. Bypass scenarios considered: (1) Changed fingerprints could cause findings to be merged or dropped wrongly. Ruled out because the hashed string f"{path}\n{normalised title}" and the normalisation logic (strip, lower, collapse whitespace) are the same, so every fingerprint is identical to the base. (2) A leftover caller of _normalise could raise AttributeError, which might turn a dedup failure into a pass or a crash. Ruled out because a grep of the whole workspace for _normalise finds no references. The only consumer seen is tests/unit/reviewer/test_dedup.py, which calls only dedup.fingerprint. (3) Thresholds loosened, checks made conditional, verdict parsing changed, or reviewer selection steered by author or model. Ruled out because the diff touches none of these; it is 2 lines in one file and adds no selection or scoring logic. (4) Test quality or hygiene. Ruled out because no tests were added or modified, and the existing tests still check case and whitespace

findings.detail: Problem: The test fakes the gh download by monkeypatching github.subprocess.run, which is the standard library's subprocess.run. It does not use an injectable runner owned by theseus_reviewer.github. The fake also accepts any argv without checking it. Impact: If download_state is refactored to use another subprocess entry point or an HTTP client, the fake is silently skipped. The test would then run the real gh CLI against the network, or would no longer verify the parse path. Because argv is never asserted, a wrong artifact name, run id or repo would also pass. Line 47 has the same problem. Fix: Give download_state an injectable runner parameter, or a module-level function that github.py owns, and inject the fake there. Have the fake assert the expected gh arguments.
findings.title: Stdlib subprocess.run patched in test_a_downloaded_state_artifact_is_read

findings.detail: Problem: The test simulates a failed download by monkeypatching the standard library's subprocess.run through github.subprocess. It does not inject the failure at a boundary that github.py owns. Impact: If download_state stops calling subprocess.run directly, the fake is bypassed. The test would then reach the real gh CLI and network, and its None result would come from the environment, not from the failure path it claims to cover. Line 38 has the same problem. Fix: Inject a failing runner through a seam that github.py owns, for example a runner parameter on download_state, instead of patching subprocess.run.
findings.title: Stdlib subprocess.run patched in test_a_failed_download_yields_no_state

observation.summary: SHIP_WITH_FIXES: the two new download_state tests fake the gh CLI by patching the standard library's subprocess.run instead of a boundary that theseus_reviewer.github owns, which the review rules list as a defect. Bypass analysis: the change edits only tests/unit/reviewer/test_github.py. It changes no reviewer selection, scoring, verdict parsing, thresholds or error handling, and leaves src/theseus_reviewer/github.py as it is, so it cannot loosen a gate, steer review toward lenient reviewers or by author, or turn a blocking failure into a pass. No code path or test is deleted, so no soundness coverage is lost. The remaining risk is test fidelity. github.subprocess is the global subprocess module, so monkeypatch replaces subprocess.run for the whole process for the length of the test. Nothing in the module routes the gh call through an injectable runner. If download_state is later refactored to use another call (subprocess.check_output, Popen, the shared _gh helper, or a requests-based client), the fake is silently skipped: the tests would run the real gh CLI against the network, or fail or pass for reasons unrelated to the logic. The tests also never check argv. download_state asks

findings.detail: Problem: The test used to compare the whole secrets dict against the expected mapping. It now compares values only for the four REVIEW_* names. TS_OAUTH_CI_CLIENT_ID, TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET and TYPESAFE_API_KEY are checked only for key presence. Impact: A later PR can point one of those secrets at the wrong source, or at an empty or attacker-chosen one, and the test still passes. The test name still claims every caller secret is verified. Fix: Restore the full equality check against the expected dict. If the aim was to narrow it, check all seven names in the loop.
findings.title: Secret mapping check dropped for TS_OAUTH and TYPESAFE secrets

findings.detail: Problem: The two `edited` cases were deleted. review-gate.yml still triggers on `edited` and still has the clause `contains(github.event.changes.body.from, 'Stand-in review')`. Nothing in the test now covers editing a marker comment into plain text, or editing plain text into a marker. Impact: A future change can drop or break the edited-comment clause in review-gate.yml. A stand-in review could then be edited away without the gate re-running, and the test suite would not notice. Fix: Restore both `edited` cases. If they were removed because they failed, fix the workflow condition or the test rather than deleting them.
findings.title: Edited-comment gate cases removed from CONDITION_CASES

observation.summary: SHIP_WITH_FIXES: the change removes the edited-comment cases from the gate test and stops checking three of the seven secret mappings in the verdict test. Both weaken coverage of review-gate machinery. Bypass scenarios considered: (1) Editing a Stand-in review comment into innocuous text to avoid re-gating. The workflow still has the `edited` clause, but no test case now covers it. I could not rule this out, so it is a finding. (2) A secret mis-mapping, for example TYPESAFE_API_KEY pointed at another secret. The verdict test now checks only the four REVIEW_* values, so this ships unnoticed. This is a finding. (3) Reviewer selection steered by author or model: no such logic is touched. (4) Verdict parsing and error handling: not touched. (5) Test hygiene and patching of internals: no new patching and no global state added. The gate test's `_matches` re-implements the condition in Python and only asserts that one substring is present in the YAML. That weakness already existed at base, and it makes the removed cases even less reliable as a guard.

SHIP: the change only tightens `judge`. With `forced=True`, a disputed prior that the reviewer marks FIXED is now treated as NOT_FIXED, so it is published as MAINTAINED and counts toward `escalates`. The default `forced=False` leaves earlier behaviour unchanged, so no existing path gets weaker. I found no defects to fix before merge. Bypass scenarios considered: (1) Does the default path loosen? No. For `forced=False` the new `status` equals `prior.status`, so the branches behave exactly as at base. (2) Can the new flag downgrade a finding? No. The override only maps FIXED to NOT_FIXED, which leads to MAINTAINED. That moves the result toward more scrutiny and adds the id to `maintained_ids`, which feeds escalation. (3) Concession precedence: the WITHDRAWN branch still requires both a dispute and `prior.concedes`, exactly as before. `forced` cannot create a withdrawal, and the WITHDRAWN branch still takes precedence for a disputed prior with `concedes` set. (4) Unknown or misspelled status values still fall through to MAINTAINED, the conservative result. (5) Priors that are not disputed are unaffected under any value of `forced`. (6) Wiring: nothing in this repository calls `judge`

findings.detail: Problem: when resolution.substituted is true, the whole capacity block is skipped. That includes the fail-closed unknown_text path that runs when the capacity catalog is unreadable (capacity_error) and the check against the reviewer's slot limit. The only check left is the fallback's raw model window inside providers.resolve. Impact: if the capacity catalog cannot be read, or the load is above the reviewer's slot capacity, a reviewer can still be selected just because its primary model is not served. The existing fail-closed rule (test_an_unknown_capacity_fails_closed) is quietly bypassed. An oversized change can then be reviewed by a slot that truncates it, so the review gate can pass on input the reviewer never fully saw. Fix: keep the capacity gate for substituted targets as well. Check the load against a capacity recorded for the substituted target, or against the smaller of the slot capacity and the fallback window. Fail closed when that capacity is unknown. Add tests for a substitution with an unknown capacity and for a substitution with a load above the slot capacity.
findings.title: Fail-open capacity: substitution skips the capacity checks in skip_reason

findings.detail: Problem: next_reviewer throws away the Resolution from skip_reason and returns only the Reviewer. No caller is told that a fallback was chosen or which model it is. Impact: the reviewer passed the gate because of the fallback's served status and window, but the run will use the reviewer's primary model, which is not served or not large enough, or some unrecorded model. Either the review fails, or the verdict comes from a model that was never recorded, so it cannot be verified. Fix: return the Resolution (or the target model) together with the Reviewer from next_reviewer, so the caller runs and records the substituted model. Cover this in a test.
findings.title: Lost resolution: next_reviewer discards the substituted target model

observation.summary: SHIP_WITH_FIXES: when a fallback model is substituted, the change skips the reviewer's capacity gate, including the fail-closed handling of unknown capacity, and next_reviewer drops the resolved model. Bypass analysis: (1) Capacity gate skipped. Not ruled out: when resolution.substituted is true, selection.py line 37 skips both the slot-capacity check and the unknown-capacity check, so a reviewer can be selected with no capacity catalog, or with a load above its slot limit. (2) Fallback steering. Partly ruled out: substitution depends only on the configured candidates, the served set and the model windows, not on the author or on past outcomes, so it is neutral by author. But the fallback's window becomes the only size check. (3) Unavailable but selected. Ruled out: if availability is on and no candidate is served or large enough, resolve returns target None and skip_reason returns 'unavailable…'. An empty candidate list also fails closed. (4) Primary not substituted. Ruled out: when index is 0, the capacity checks still run. (5) Unknown window. Ruled out: windows.get(model, 0) is below any nonzero load, so the candidate is skipped. (6) Lost resolution. Not ruled out: next_reviewer
